children: is estimating a bill of about €16 billion ($18.6 billion) for a sweeping restructuring that could involve tens of thousands of job cuts and the closure or repurposing of German factories, Reuters reported on Thursday, citing a person familiar with the matter.
The cost estimate highlights the scale of the challenge confronting Europe’s biggest automaker as it tries to reduce excess capacity and improve its competitive position. Volkswagen
is contending with stronger Chinese rivals, higher tariffs, and weaker economics across parts of its manufacturing network.

Under an agreement reached last week, the company is considering alternatives for four German sites that are expected to lose vehicle programs over the next decade. The plan would increase the number of positions targeted for elimination by about 50,000 beyond previously announced reductions.
Production exits at Emden and Zwickau are each expected to cost roughly €1 billion, while measures involving the Neckarsulm and Hanover facilities could require about €2 billion apiece.
is also setting aside about €10 billion for costs linked to reducing its global workforce by as many as 60,000 employees.

title: Volkswagen puts €16B estimate on restructuring drive
